{{COI|date=May 2017}}

'''Martin Winter''' (born 7 August 1965) is a German chemist and materials scientist from [[Osnabrück]]. His research in the field of electrochemical energy storage and conversion focuses on the development of new materials, components and cell designs for batteries and [[supercapacitor]]s, [[Lithium-ion battery|lithium ion batteries]] and [[Lithium battery|lithium metal batteries]].

== Career and research ==
Winter graduated in chemistry from the [[University of Münster]] (Westfälische Wilhelms-Universität Münster) in 1992. He obtained his Ph.D. (1995) under the professorship of [[Jürgen O. Besenhard]] and worked as Post-Doctoral Research Fellow with Prof. Petr Novak at the [[Paul Scherrer Institute]] in Switzerland. After [[habilitation]] in 1999, Winter held a full professorship and the chair at the Institute of Chemical Technology of Inorganic Materials at the TU Graz. In 2008 he came back to Münster to hold the professorship for “Materials Science, Energy and Electrochemistry” at the Institute of Physical Chemistry at the University of Münster. The full professorship developed from an endowed full professorship funded by the companies [[Volkswagen]], [[Evonik Industries]] and Chemetall (today [[Albemarle Corporation|Albemarle]]) from 2008 to 2012. He was a full professor of “Applied Materials Science for Electrochemical Energy Storage and Conversion” between 2008 and 2016 and has been a full professor of “Materials Science, Energy and Electrochemistry” since 2016.

In 2008 Winter founded the MEET Battery Research Center at the University of Münster. Until today he is the scientific director of MEET, which stands for „Münster Electrochemical Energy Technology“.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.uni-muenster.de/MEET/en/index.shtml|title=MEET – Homepage MEET|website=www.uni-muenster.de|accessdate=20 December 2021}}</ref> Since January 2015 he is also the founding director of the Helmholtz-Institute Münster (HI MS) “Ionics in Energy Storage”,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.helmholtz.de/en/about-us/who-we-are/|title=Who we are|website=Helmholtz-Gemeinschaft Deutscher Forschungszentren|accessdate=20 December 2021}}</ref> which is part of the Institute of Energy and Climate Research (IEK) of [[Forschungszentrum Jülich]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fz-juelich.de/portal/EN/Home/home_node.html|title=Forschungszentrum Jülich – portal|website=www.fz-juelich.de|accessdate=20 December 2021}}</ref>

His expertise in battery research led to diverse advisory positions and activities. As the chairman of the Advisory Board of German Battery Research by the [[Federal Ministry of Education and Research (Germany)|Federal Ministry of Education and Research (BMBF)]], former spokesman of the Innovation Alliance LIB2015, spokesman of the battery initiative Batterie2020 of the BMBF, head of the Battery Competence Center (ElektroMobilität NRW) and member of the "Electromobility" expert council of the North Rhine-Westphalian state government he represents the German battery research on national and international level. Winter is President of the International Meeting on Lithium Batteries (IMLB), chairman of the [[International Battery Materials Association]] (IBA), Fellow of the [[International Society of Electrochemistry]] (ISE) and of the [[Electrochemical Society]] (ECS), where he is also board member of the Battery Division. He has published more than 500 articles in journals, books and proceedings and has filed ca. 70 patent applications (2018).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.uni-muenster.de/MEET/en/team/winter.shtml|title=List of publications of Martin Winter on the website of MEET Battery Research Center, University Münster}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
Winter is a highly cited author as recognized by [[Thomson Reuters|ISI (Thomson Reuters)]], [[Shanghai ranking|The Shanghai Ranking]], and [[Elsevier|Elsevier Scopus]]. Among more than 40 awards and recognitions, he holds the Carl Wagner Memorial Award of the [[Electrochemical Society]] (ECS), has been the recipient of the Research and Technology awards of both, the [[Electrochemical Society|ECS]] and the International Battery Materials Association (IBA) and was recognized by the “[[Braunschweiger Forschungspreis]]”. In 2018 he was awarded the [[Order of Merit of the Federal Republic of Germany|Federal Cross of Merit]] 1st class. Winter is [[Honorary professor|Honorary Professor]] at the [[National Taiwan University of Science and Technology]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.uni-muenster.de/MEET/presse/honoraryprofessorshiptaiwantech.html|title=Honorary Professorship Taiwan Tech|last=Technology|first=Westfälische Wilhelms-Universität Münster, MEET – Münster Electrochemical Energy|website=www.uni-muenster.de|language=de|access-date=10 September 2018}}</ref> (Taipei, Taiwan) and the National Cheng Kung University in Tainan (Taiwan).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.uni-muenster.de/MEET/en/presse/honorarychairprofessorncku.html|title=HonoraryChairProfessorNCKU|last=Technology|first=Westfälische Wilhelms-Universität Münster, MEET – Münster Electrochemical Energy|website=www.uni-muenster.de|language=en|access-date=1 October 2018}}</ref>
